A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same hypergraph Ricci-flow clustering work. Their complete main texts, figures, tables, equations and appendices are readable, allowing retained, relocated and newly added material to be matched reliably.

before.justification: v1 reports original synthetic clustering experiments in Figure 5, Ricci-method results on real datasets in Table 2, and computational measurements in Figure 6.

after.justification: v2 retains original synthetic and real-data experiments and adds runtime comparisons and original hyperparameter and threshold analyses in Section 4.3 and Appendix C.

M1.justification: The transport, aggregation, flow-update and trimming pipeline remains. However, v2 Equation 3 replaces the shared/nonshared alpha-split edge measure with normalized weights over the full star; the earlier alpha=0 construction survives as Equation 4 for Proposition 1. Section 3.1 also removes the inverse-summed hyperedge-contribution weighting option.

E1.justification: All seven real datasets and the synthetic clustering families remain. Synthetic cardinality coverage changes modestly: Figure 5 replaces cross-community sizes 2, 3, 4 and 5 with 2, 4 and 6. Several size-3 and size-5 scenarios remain in Appendix C, so their disappearance from the main figure is not wholesale removal.

E2.justification: The real-data NMI comparison retains Node2Vec, DGI, GRACE, S2-HHGR, TriCL and Modularity. v2 additionally compares Modularity against both Ricci methods for real-data runtime in Table 2; v1's computational comparison only contrasts the two Ricci methods.

E3.justification: The main NMI metric, 20 flow iterations, synthetic 100-node/two-community setup and main threshold-selection rules remain. New experiments introduce controlled parameter combinations, comparisons between label-optimal and graph/hypergraph-modularity thresholds, and 20-iteration runtime measurements on four real datasets. Explicit p=1 and alpha=0.5 values replace unspecified library defaults in the documentation, without establishing a change from the earlier implementation.

E4.justification: New Section 4.3 and Appendix C substantially expand sensitivity analysis beyond v1's brief assertions. Figures S.2-S.6 test p, alpha, weighting and aggregation interactions; Tables S.2-S.3 examine joint parameter effects on NTU2012; Tables S.4-S.5 quantify threshold-selection effects on NTU2012 and Zoo.

E5.justification: Section 4.1 changes the reported averaging from ten random hypergraph generations to five. Figure 5 newly displays shaded bands, although their statistical meaning is not defined. The synthetic timing experiment retains averaging over five initializations.

E6.justification: NTU2012's reported NMI changes from 82.3 to 76.3 for N-Ricci and from 80.9 to 77.6 for E-Ricci, reversing their ordering; other entries in the main accuracy table remain unchanged. Figure 5 is revised, and new runtime and sensitivity results substantially expand the findings. These revisions do not establish controlled performance gains or losses because the earlier defaults and changed synthetic settings are not fully matched.

T1.justification: v2 generalizes the displayed node-measure definition with distance decay p and revises the main edge-measure definition. Proposition 1 retains its recurrence and shared-edge exclusion assumption, expressed through Equation 4 rather than alpha=0. Appendix A adds distance-based optimality arguments and corrects the first transport target, without introducing a new theorem.

C1.justification: The abstract and principal introduction/conclusion claims remain: edge transport through the line expansion provides a complementary hypergraph clustering approach, particularly useful for large hyperedges and certain community structures. Added experiments and qualifications do not redefine the main contribution.

C2.justification: v2 replaces broad assertions of weak parameter sensitivity with substantial qualifications about weighting/aggregation interactions and extreme node-alpha instability. It adds explicit limits on transferring Ollivier-curvature theory and sign interpretability, explains runtime disadvantages for large node stars, and discusses threshold-dependent clustering granularity. Appendix C also reports numerical instability for p=2 on NTU2012.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents node-measure defaults, gives constructive synthetic hyperedge-sampling instructions, and specifies the new sensitivity experiments. It replaces the code/data pointer from OlympioH/Ricci_curv_hyp with AnonRicciHG/Ricci_curv_HG. The principal software packages and hardware description were already present in v1.

R1.justification: v2 adds references including Sreejith et al., Iyer et al., Tian et al., Cushing et al. and Van Der Hoorn et al., expanding discussion of alternative curvatures, line-graph clustering and graph-curvature convergence. The central positioning relative to earlier hypergraph and Ricci-flow methods remains.

P1.justification: Most existing exposition and the main section sequence are retained, with local language corrections and expanded explanations. Dataset descriptions move from Section 4.2 to Appendix B, a dedicated hyperparameter section and Appendix C are added, and publication/contact text changes. This is limited reorganization rather than wholesale rewriting.

P2.justification: v2 adopts a substantially different publication layout and rebuilds Figure 5 from sixteen small panels into twelve larger panels with revised legends and shaded bands. It adds five supplementary figures, four analysis tables and a runtime table, while relocating dataset statistics and retaining the proof illustration as Figure S.1.

improvement.justification: Section 4.3 and Appendix C address an important weakness in v1: parameter-insensitivity assertions lacked systematic supporting evidence. The new analyses establish consequential parameter interactions and quantify practical threshold-selection losses, while runtime comparisons and explicit theoretical limitations make applicability substantially easier to assess. Fewer synthetic repetitions and undefined shaded bands remain weaknesses, but the gains in experimental support and qualification clearly outweigh them.
